### A3 — reproduced three-demo shortcut that fails on the query

The base generator is deterministic and its individual examples were strong in
a 600-sample probe (200 per easy/medium/hard): 600/600 valid, 600/600 unique
inputs, 600/600 unique outputs, 600/600 correct descending row order, 600/600
locally compacted rows, and 240/240 exact profile override cases. All three
canonical pairs were accepted and matched by the Python mirror.

The lesson-level probe nevertheless found rolling three-demo windows that fail
to refute a plausible canonical-compatible rival:

- easy: 23 windows;
- medium: 18 windows;
- hard: 16 windows.

The exact retained episode is easy difficulty:

| role | seed | sample index |
|---|---:|---:|
| demo 1 | 101844 | 719 |
| demo 2 | 101941 | 720 |
| demo 3 | 102038 | 721 |
| query | 102135 | 722 |

Every pair is generated-domain input and passes the target validator. The rival
`deduplicate_then_left` removes repeated values before left-compaction. It fits
all three demonstrations and all canonical pairs because none contains a
repeated foreground value. The query contains a repeated `1`; the authoritative
rule preserves it, while the rival deletes one copy. Supported Racket application
on all four inputs matches the recorded generator outputs.

### T1 — isolated task-test portability defect

The official task-test runner executed 12 tests: 11 passed and one failed before
its semantic assertion because the test opened a guessed path,
`generators/1a2f04639576/data/canonical/puzzles.jsonl`, that is absent from the
isolated runtime. This is a test/tooling portability finding, not evidence that
the target's rule failed. Full traceback and runtime manifest are in
`checks/audits/1a2f04639576/task-tests/result.json`.

No audit-target or shared file was changed.
